correctness.rationale: The original two-variable differential equations and all parameter inequalities were reconstructed. The saddle has one stable eigenvalue and one unstable eigenvalue, giving a unique graph whose strict upper and moving-lower barriers ensure continuation to all compositions. Its upper-end limit is forced to the lower Allee root by a nonintegrable 1/(1-x) singularity. Monotone strategies plus an asymptotically autonomous scalar resource law give the three exhaustive long-run alternatives; scalar uniqueness prevents crossing of the separator. Two scalar comparisons rigorously establish strict greed ordering and the explicit uniform O(w) error estimate. A standard-library script passes 60 deterministic parameter-pair tests, bounds, a source-parameter comparison, and opposite-basin trajectory examples. Finite sampling supports but does not establish the theorem.

value.rationale: This is the exact global divide between irreversible collapse and resource persistence in a motivating Allee common-pool game, not merely an equilibrium sign check. Its strict dependence on behavioral response speed supplies a mathematically important distinction obscured by a line segment between fixed-strategy tipping points. The explicit uniform O(w) control gives a useful approximation guarantee across every initial cooperator fraction, and the work addresses a natural bistability quantity rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
